prs.title: Enhanced Pagination Performance for High-Volume Audit Logs

review_comments.body:
[P0] Negative slicing on Django QuerySets will crash

`OptimizedCursorPaginator` attempts `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `cursor.offset < 0` and `enable_advanced_features` is true, but Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing/slicing and raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.` This will cause 500s for any request that produces a negative offset.

[P0] Possible AttributeError when organization_context.member is None

`enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences `organization_context.member` without a null check. If `member` can be `None` for the current user/org context, this will raise at runtime; guard it (e.g. `request.user.is_superuser or (organization_context.member and organization_context.member.has_global_access)`).

reviews.body: Two concrete runtime issues are introduced by the optimized pagination path: (1) `organization_context.member` is optional and is dereferenced without a null-check in the audit logs endpoint, which can raise an AttributeError for token/anon auth contexts, and (2) allowing negative offsets in `OptimizedCursorPaginator` will crash Django QuerySet slicing with `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` when a negative cursor offset is supplied.

prs.title: Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert

review_comments.body:
[P1] BasePaginator can still pass a negative start index for prev cursors

`BasePaginator.get_result()` now clamps `offset` only when `cursor.is_prev` is false; when `cursor.is_prev` is true it uses `start_offset = offset` unchanged. If the decoded cursor contains a negative `offset`, this will attempt `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start and raise `AssertionError` instead of returning a controlled pagination error. Validate/reject negative offsets at cursor decode time or in `get_result()`.

reviews.body: The performance-oriented cursor changes introduce a concrete failure mode: negative offsets can reach Django QuerySet slicing and raise AssertionError, producing a 500 for crafted cursors (notably on prev cursors). Clamping/rejecting negative offsets should make the optimization safe.

prs.title: feat(upsampling) - Support upsampled error count with performance optimizations

review_comments.body:
[P1] Test authenticates as a different user than `self.user` due to shadowing

In `setUp()`, `self.login_as(user=self.user)` runs before `self.user = self.create_user()`. `self.user` is a cached_property on the base test case, so the first access creates and authenticates one user, then the later assignment overwrites `self.user` with a different instance. This makes the test’s authenticated user diverge from later references to `self.user`, which can hide permission issues or introduce flakiness when future assertions depend on the logged-in identity.

[P1] Upsampling eligibility check uses the wrong dataset variable

`is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(...)` is called with the outer-scope `dataset` variable, but `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` (the dataset actually used for the query). When `get_event_stats_factory` calls `_get_event_stats` with a different dataset than the outer `dataset` (e.g. split datasets), the upsampling decision can be made against the wrong dataset, leading to incorrect application (or skipping) of the `count() -> upsampled_count()` transformation.

[P1] `upsampled_count` should likely be marked private to avoid user-triggered Snuba failures

`upsampled_count()` directly references `sample_weight`, which (per the helper’s own assumptions) is only present for error events in allowlisted projects. Because this `SnQLFunction` is not marked `private=True`, callers could invoke `upsampled_count()` in arbitrary discover queries/projects, which can result in Snuba column-not-found errors when `sample_weight` is absent. If this function is intended only for internal substitution of `count()` when eligibility has been checked, it should be private like other internal-only functions in this registry.

reviews.body: Found three concrete correctness issues: dataset mismatch can cause missed/incorrect upsampling in the stats endpoint, `upsampled_count()` being non-private can let users trigger Snuba column errors, and the new test’s `self.user` shadowing can mask auth-related failures.

review_comments.body:
[P0] OAuth state parameter is predictable/deterministic

The `state` parameter for the OAuth flow is set to `pipeline.signature`, which is derived from pipeline view class names and is constant across users/sessions (it’s even asserted in tests as `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`). A predictable `state` defeats CSRF protection for OAuth; it should be a per-flow cryptographically random value stored in the pipeline/session and validated on callback.

[P1] Potential KeyError when reading integration.metadata['sender']['login']

The comparison against `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes those keys always exist. Older/edge integrations may not have `sender` (or `login`) in metadata, which would raise `KeyError` and crash the installation flow; use `.get()`/guards and treat missing data as an invalid request (or fall back to a safer check).

[P1] test_github_user_mismatch likely fails due to missing webhook secret setup

The test posts to `/extensions/github/webhook/` with `HTTP_X_HUB_SIGNATURE=...` and asserts a 204, but it doesn’t configure `github-app.webhook-secret`. If the option defaults to an empty string, signature verification will fail and the endpoint will return 401. Set `options.set('github-app.webhook-secret', <secret>)` and compute the signature for the mutated payload (or mock signature verification) to make this test deterministic.

reviews.body: The GitHub installation hardening adds useful checks, but OAuth `state` is deterministic (undermining CSRF protection), the new sender-login comparison can raise `KeyError` for integrations without `metadata['sender']`, and the new mismatch test likely fails because webhook signature verification isn’t configured for the mutated payload.

review_comments.body:
[P2] `age` validation allows negative values

`BrowserReportSerializer.age` lacks `min_value=0` while `timestamp` enforces non-negative values. `age` represents elapsed milliseconds per the Reporting API and should also be non-negative; allowing negative ages through validation can lead to accepting invalid reports.

[P0] Incorrect error event to ID mapping due to dict key mismatch

`fetch_error_details` uses `zip(error_ids, events.values())` after `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`, but `get_multi` returns a dict keyed by `node_id` (hashed), not by the original `error_id`. Iterating `events.values()` and zipping with `error_ids` can misassociate IDs with payloads (and drop/misorder items). Instead, iterate `for error_id, node_id in zip(error_ids, node_ids): data = events.get(node_id)` (or build a mapping) so each `error_id` pulls the correct event payload.

[P2] Analytics event recorded before feature gate check

`analytics.record()` runs before the `features.has('organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble', ...)` check, so requests from orgs/users without the feature enabled will still emit `preprod_artifact.api.assemble`. This can skew analytics and adds work on the disabled path; record only after the feature check passes (or include an explicit flag indicating gated/denied).

reviews.body: Validated 3 actionable issues: replay error context can misassociate error IDs to nodestore payloads due to zipping against dict values, browser reporting accepts negative `age`, and preprod assemble analytics is recorded on the feature-disabled path. The wildcard import concern looks intentional for analytics registration and is not a concrete bug.

prs.title: Span Buffer Multiprocess Enhancement with Health Monitoring

review_comments.body:
[P2] Inconsistent shard tag key across metrics

The flusher uses `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` for `spans.buffer.flusher.produce`/`spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` but `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` for `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce`. This inconsistency will split aggregations and make dashboards harder to query; use a single consistent tag key.

[P1] Off-by-one in flusher restart limit check

`_ensure_processes_alive` checks `if self.process_restarts[process_index] > MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` and only increments the counter afterwards, which allows one extra restart (MAX+1) before raising. Increment before checking, or change the comparison to `>=`, to enforce the intended cap.

[P2] Patched sleep makes the intended wait a no-op and can hide a race

`monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` makes the later `time.sleep(0.1)` a no-op, even though the comment says it is giving flusher threads time after changing `current_drift`. The test currently relies on `step.join()` timing, and `join()` sets `stopped.value = True`, so under unlucky scheduling the flusher can observe the stop flag before completing a flush iteration. Prefer an explicit condition-based wait (e.g. poll until `messages` is populated or until a metric/state indicates a flush) or remove the misleading sleep/comment.

reviews.body: The multiprocess flusher refactor looks broadly sound, but there are a couple of correctness/operability issues: the restart limit check is off-by-one and shard-related metric tagging is inconsistent. The updated test also contains a no-op sleep that may mask a subtle shutdown race, which could lead to flaky behavior.

review_comments.body:
[P0] `queued` default timestamp is evaluated at import time

`queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the module is imported, so every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` will share the same stale timestamp. Use `dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so `timezone.now()` runs per instance.

reviews.body: One concrete bug: `AssignmentSource.queued` uses an import-time default, so instances can share a stale timestamp unless switched to a per-instance default factory. The rest of the changes look consistent with the new assignment-source threading for assignee sync.

prs.title: ref(crons): Reorganize incident creation / issue occurrence logic

review_comments.body:
[P1] Incident can trigger before reaching failure_issue_threshold

When `failure_issue_threshold > 1`, the code slices up to `failure_issue_threshold` check-ins but never verifies it actually retrieved that many; if a new monitor has fewer total check-ins than the threshold and all are failures, `any(status==OK)` will be false and an incident will be created prematurely. Add a guard like `if len(previous_checkins) < failure_issue_threshold: return False` before creating the incident.

[P1] get_monitor_environment_context returns unmodified config

This function copies `monitor_environment.monitor.config` into `config` and updates `config["schedule_type"]`, but then returns `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the original) instead of the local `config`. As a result, the schedule_type display transformation never takes effect in the emitted context.

reviews.body: Two correctness issues in the refactor: the monitor context returns the wrong config object (dropping the schedule_type display override), and incident creation can occur before the configured failure threshold is actually reached when there are fewer historical check-ins than the threshold.

prs.title: feat(workflow_engine): Add in hook for producing occurrences from the stateful detector

review_comments.body:
[P0] MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and will crash on instantiation

`MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` but doesn't implement its required abstract API (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). Since `Detector.detector_handler` instantiates via `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, any detector using `MetricAlertFire` will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class ...` at runtime. Either implement the required methods or keep this handler on `DetectorHandler` until the stateful implementation is ready.

reviews.body: The stateful detector refactor looks coherent, but `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was switched to `StatefulDetectorHandler` without implementing required abstract methods, which will raise a `TypeError` when the handler is instantiated for the `metric_alert_fire` group type.
